companyDescription: Vertically integrated Earth-observation satellite company — designs, builds & operates its own smallsat constellation for daily sub-meter global imaging; now scaling into government/defense (new President is a former NGA director)
priceNote: Prior same-day draft used $4.62 — live price $5.59 is +21.0% higher, confirmed genuine (not a stale-cache artifact). The gap traces to real news the draft missed: the Sep 8 appointment of VADM (Ret.) Frank Whitworth, former NGA director, as President drove a +15.73% single-day pop, on top of the Sep 3 SynMax maritime-imagery partnership news. Today's -7.52% looks like profit-taking after that run, not new negative news.
summary: Satellogic's Merlin constellation begins launching in October 2026 (two NewSat Mark VI satellites with inter-satellite-link tech plus one NewSat Mark V), the first hard revenue-unlock event since the company guided to a ~$1B Space Systems pipeline. Since the last snapshot, two real catalysts landed: SynMax was named exclusive maritime partner for Merlin-constellation imagery (Sep 3), and Vice Admiral (Ret.) Frank Whitworth — former director of the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency — was appointed President (Sep 8), a strong signal on government/defense scaling that the market rewarded with a +15.73% pop. Q2 2026 revenue grew 259% YoY to $15.9M with the company's first-ever positive operating income. Consensus target is now $10.20 (5 analysts, Strong Buy, high $11/low $9), +82.5% from $5.59 — narrower than the prior report's $8.90-15 range but confirms real analyst conviction survives the run. Base case (+55%) assumes a 3-4 month re-rating horizon through launch success and first commissioning data, not the 14-day North Star window — well above the core lane's realized 14d P75 of +6.6%, so read the gap as a horizon difference, not optimism bias.

catalysts.name: Merlin Constellation Launch (2 NewSat Mark VI + 1 Mark V)
catalysts.description: First Merlin-class satellites launch in October 2026, fully customer-funded. Success unlocks the ~$1B Space Systems pipeline and the Q4 2026 revenue contribution management has already guided to. SynMax now holds exclusive maritime-imagery rights on Merlin data (announced Sep 3, 2026).

catalysts.name: Defense/Government Scale-Up Under New President
catalysts.description: VADM (Ret.) Frank Whitworth, former NGA director, appointed President effective Sep 8, 2026 — a strong signal for government/defense business development. ONR Slingshot III program also expanded (six additional Mark VI satellites over 18 months).

risks: Launch delay or anomaly would push revenue recognition and could trigger a sharp de-rate — satellite_launch is the most volatile catalyst type in the feedback set (medianMAE -19.4%, n=8) and is also the feedback set's STRONGEST performer on median excess vs SPY (+7.4pp, n=8) — high variance in both directions

The stock has already run +21% into this refresh on real news (Whitworth appointment, SynMax deal) — some of the launch catalyst's upside may already be partly priced in ahead of the actual October launch
Balance sheet depends on continued customer prepayments/financing — a hawkish Fed (rates hiked to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16) raises the cost of the next capital round if Merlin slips
Thin analyst coverage (5 names, target range $9-$11) means the consensus target could reprice quickly on any single revision
Sub-$1.2B market cap and a still-relatively-low float drive outsized volatility in both directions, as today's -7.52% single-day move shows

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16, 2026 (first hike since 2023) on elevated inflation; futures price ~4.2% by Dec 2026. Next FOMC is Oct 27-28, 2026 — after Merlin's launch window, so it shouldn't collide with the catalyst itself, but it raises the cost of Satellogic's next financing round if launch slips.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Elevated inflation is the stated reason for the hike, not a growth scare — risk-on small caps can still work if the launch succeeds, but the discount-rate headwind on still-scaling names is real, even with Q2's first positive operating income.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Space/Earth-observation names have re-rated hard on SpaceX-IPO spillover, launch-cadence news, and defense-scaling hires (Satellogic's own Whitworth appointment) in 2026; a hawkish Fed is a headwind to that multiple but hasn't broken the sector trend yet.
macroRisk.summary: HIGH macro risk given Satellogic's financing-dependent balance sheet in a renewed hiking cycle, but the launch catalyst is company-specific and largely macro-independent — thesis break is a launch failure, not a rate move.

entryStrategy.verdict: Measured median at-catalyst return across the core catalyst lane is -6.9% (n=54) — buying at today's $5.59 is not the default entry; the $4.70-5.00 zone (today's pullback) is preferred. Satellite_launch is the feedback set's strongest catalyst type (+7.4pp median excess vs SPY, n=8) and Merlin is the first hard revenue-unlock event in Satellogic's public history, now backed by a credible defense-scaling hire — buy the dip, size small given binary launch risk.

catalystSpot.preRunup: Space/EO names in this sector typically drift up into a confirmed launch window as pre-sales and pipeline commentary build; Satellogic itself has already shown this pattern twice this month (SynMax deal Sep 3, Whitworth appointment Sep 8) ahead of the actual October launch

postWin.note: Real 2026 comps: Planet Labs +16% on raised guidance + 3 new satellite launches (Jun 2026), AST SpaceMobile +20% on deployment progress (May 2026), Rocket Lab +34% single-day on a record launch deal (treat as the upper bound, not typical). skill-feedback.json's satellite_launch bucket measures a lower avgMaxGain of 6.1% (n=8) over its fixed 14d window — the gap is a measurement-horizon artifact, not a contradiction.

postLose.note: No direct Satellogic launch-failure precedent; proxied from the satellite_launch bucket's own medianMAE (-19.4%, n=8) and the general pattern of launch delays compressing sentiment until the next confirmed window.
